items.title: Rokeby Venus
items.file: Diego Velázquez - Rokeby Venus.jpg
items.why: Slashed seven times with a meat cleaver in 1914 by the suffragette Mary Richardson, in protest at the arrest of Emmeline Pankhurst.

items.title: Las Meninas
items.file: Las Meninas, by Diego Velázquez, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg
items.why: The painter is in his own picture, looking out at what he is painting, which is where you are standing. The king and queen appear only in a mirror.

items.title: The Third of May 1808
items.file: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes - Los fusilamientos del tres de mayo - 1814.jpg
items.why: The man in white throws his arms out in a crucifixion pose; the firing squad has no faces. Goya invented the modern image of atrocity here.

items.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
items.file: Francisco de Goya, Saturno devorando a su hijo (1819-1823).jpg
items.why: One of the Black Paintings — Goya put these straight onto the plaster walls of his own house, for nobody, in his seventies and deaf.

items.title: Venus of Urbino
items.file: Tiziano's Venere di Urbino (from The History BLog).jpg
items.why: Mark Twain called it the foulest painting in the world. She meets your eye instead of averting it, which is most of the difference between this and a goddess.

items.title: The Death of Socrates
items.file: The Death of Socrates MET DP-13139-001.jpg
items.why: He is still lecturing, one hand reaching for the hemlock without looking at it. Plato sits at the foot of the bed as an old man, though he was young at the time and, by his own account, not there.

items.title: The Oath of the Horatii
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Le Serment des Horaces - Jacques-Louis David - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3692 ; MR 1432.jpg
items.why: Three brothers swear to die for Rome while the women collapse at the right — the composition splits the canvas into duty and grief.

items.title: The Death of Marat
items.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
items.file: Jacques-Louis David - Marat assassinated - Google Art Project 2.jpg
items.why: Painted by a friend and political ally within months of the murder. It is propaganda, and it is one of the great paintings.

items.title: The Swing
items.file: Fragonard, The Swing.jpg
items.why: The patron’s brief survives: he wanted himself placed where he could see up her skirts. Fragonard obliged, and added the flying shoe.

items.title: The Gleaners
items.file: Jean-François Millet - Gleaners - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Three women taking the leavings after harvest — a legal right of the poorest. Painting them at this scale was read at the time as dangerous.

items.title: The Raft of the Medusa
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: JEAN LOUIS THÉODORE GÉRICAULT - La Balsa de la Medusa (Museo del Louvre, 1818-19).jpg
items.why: A current scandal painted at the scale of history painting. Géricault interviewed survivors and had the actual carpenter build him a model of the raft.

items.title: The Ambassadors
items.file: Hans Holbein the Younger - The Ambassadors - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: The smear across the floor resolves into a skull if you stand at the right-hand edge and look along the surface. Everything else in the picture is worldly success.

items.title: Whistler's Mother
items.file: Whistlers Mother high res.jpg
items.why: Its actual title is *Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1*. Whistler insisted the subject was the arrangement, not his mother.

items.title: American Gothic
items.file: Grant Wood - American Gothic (1930).jpg
items.why: The pair are a farmer and his daughter, not his wife, and the models were the artist's dentist and his own sister. Iowa hated it.

items.title: David with the Head of Goliath
items.file: David with the Head of Goliath-Caravaggio (1610).jpg

items.title: David with the Head of Goliath
items.file: David with the Head of Goliath-Caravaggio (c.1606-7).jpg

items.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
items.file: Judith Beheading Holofernes - Caravaggio.jpg

items.title: Medusa
items.file: Caravaggio - Medusa - Google Art Project.jpg

items.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
items.file: Caravaggio — The Calling of Saint Matthew.jpg
items.why: A shaft of light does the work a halo would have done. Which man at the table is actually Matthew is still argued over.

items.title: The Hay Wain
items.file: John Constable - The Hay Wain (1821).jpg
items.why: Ignored in England, it won a gold medal in Paris in 1824 and changed French landscape painting.

items.title: Ophelia
items.file: John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Millais painted the river first and the figure after; his model lay in a bath of water kept warm by lamps until the lamps went out and she caught a serious chill.

items.title: The Blue Boy
items.collection: The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens
items.file: Thomas Gainsborough - The Blue Boy (c. 1770).jpg
items.why: Partly an argument with Reynolds, who had lectured that cold colours should never dominate a picture. Gainsborough made blue the entire painting.

items.title: Liberty Leading the People
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: La Liberté guidant le peuple - Eugène Delacroix - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 129 - après restauration 2024.jpg
items.why: The bare-breasted figure is not a person but an allegory, and the man in the top hat beside her is often taken for the painter himself.

items.title: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
items.file: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Georges Seurat, 1884.jpg
items.why: Two years of work in dots of unmixed colour, on the theory that the eye would blend them. Note that almost nobody in the crowd is looking at anybody else.

ref.what: Sunday in the Park with George

items.title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
items.file: Gauguin - Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? (1897-98).jpg
items.why: Painted in Tahiti after a suicide attempt and intended as his testament. It reads right to left, from the infant to the old woman.

items.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
items.file: Renoir, Pierre-Auguste - Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette, 1876.jpg
items.why: Sunday afternoon dancing in Montmartre, painted at the scale of a history picture. Critics complained that the dappled light made the dancers look spotted with grease.

items.title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
items.file: Un bar aux Folies-Bergère d'E. Manet (Fondation Vuitton, Paris) (33539037428).jpg
items.why: The mirror is wrong, and deliberately. Her reflection is shunted far to the right, and the man she is serving ought to be standing where you are.

items.title: Luncheon on the Grass
items.file: Edouard Manet - Luncheon on the Grass - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: The nude was not the scandal — nude goddesses were fine. The scandal was that she is an ordinary woman at a picnic, looking straight at you.

ref.what: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe, after Manet

items.title: Olympia
items.file: Edouard Manet - Olympia - Google Art Project 3.jpg
items.why: Same offence, worse: a courtesan, not a Venus, and she is not remotely ashamed. It had to be hung high to keep it from being attacked.

items.title: Netherlandish Proverbs
items.file: Pieter Bruegel (der Ältere) (ca. 1525 - 1569) - Die niederländischen Sprichwörter - 1720 - Gemäldegalerie.jpg
items.why: More than a hundred proverbs staged literally in one village, including armed men banging their heads against a brick wall.

items.title: The Hunters in the Snow
items.file: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Hunters in the Snow (Winter) - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: One of a series on the months of the year. The hunters are coming home with almost nothing — a single fox between them.

items.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
items.file: Friedrich, Caspar David - Wanderer über dem Nebelmeer.jpg
items.why: The founding image of Romantic solitude, and it works by showing you a back. You cannot see his face, so you occupy him.

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.file: Sandro Botticelli - La nascita di Venere - Google Art Project - edited.jpg
items.why: She is not being born but arriving, blown ashore on a shell. Painted on canvas when Florence still expected panel, which is part of why it survived.

items.title: Primavera
items.file: Sandro Botticelli - La Primavera - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Read it right to left: the wind god seizes a nymph who transforms, mid-picture, into the flower-strewn figure beside her. Five centuries on, nobody agrees what the whole thing means.

items.title: Impression, Sunrise
items.file: Monet - Impression, Sunrise.jpg
items.why: A critic used its title to mock the whole group as mere "Impressionists". They took the insult and kept it.

items.title: View of Toledo
items.file: View of Toledo MET DP349564.jpg

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.file: Das Jüngste Gericht (Memling).jpg
items.why: Saint Bartholomew holds his own flayed skin, and the face on the skin is Michelangelo’s. The nudes were painted over with drapery after his death.

items.title: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
items.file: Turner - Rain, Steam and Speed - National Gallery file.jpg
items.why: A hare is running along the track ahead of the train. It is easy to miss, and it is the entire point of the picture.

items.title: The Fighting Temeraire
items.file: Turner, J. M. W. - The Fighting Téméraire tugged to her last Berth to be broken.jpg
items.why: A veteran of Trafalgar towed by a squat steam tug to be broken up. Turner made the sun set behind it in the wrong direction for the geography.

items.title: The Starry Night
items.file: Van Gogh - Starry Night - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Painted from the window of the asylum at Saint-Rémy, from memory and in daylight. The village below is not the one outside; he added it.

items.title: The Potato Eaters
items.file: De aardappeleters - s0005V1962 - Van Gogh Museum.jpg
items.why: Van Gogh thought this his best work. He wanted the colour of "a really dusty potato, unpeeled", and he got it.

items.title: Café Terrace at Night
items.file: Van Gogh - Terrace of a Café at Night (Place du Forum) 1888.jpg
items.why: His first night sky full of stars — and there is no black anywhere in it. The dark is built entirely from deep blues and greens.

items.title: Sistine Madonna
items.file: Raphael - The Sistine Madonna - Google Arts & Culture.jpg
items.why: The two bored cherubs leaning on the frame at the bottom have been cropped out and reproduced more often than everything above them put together.

items.title: The Kiss
items.file: The Kiss - Gustav Klimt - Google Cultural Institute.jpg
items.why: Gold leaf, laid on like a Byzantine icon. Look at the fabric: his rectangles, her circles — the pattern does the work the faces do not.

items.title: Mona Lisa
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci, from C2RMF natural color.jpg
items.why: Unremarkable for centuries — it became the most famous painting on earth after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 and the empty wall drew bigger crowds than the picture had.

items.title: Lady with an Ermine
items.file: Lady with an Ermine - Leonardo da Vinci - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Cecilia Gallerani, mistress of Leonardo’s employer Ludovico Sforza — whose emblem was an ermine, so the animal is a pun as well as a symbol. The flat black background was added centuries later by another hand.

items.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
items.file: An Experiment on a Bird in an Air Pump by Joseph Wright of Derby, 1768.jpg

items.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
items.file: Artemisia Gentileschi - Giuditta decapita Oloferne - Google Art Project-Adjust.jpg

items.title: Self-Portrait with Fur-Trimmed Robe
items.file: Dürer Alte Pinakothek.jpg

items.title: The Night Watch
items.file: La ronda de noche, por Rembrandt van Rijn.jpg
items.why: Not a night scene — the darkness is varnish. It was also cut down in 1715 to fit a wall, so the composition you see is off-centre by force.

items.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
items.file: Rembrandt - The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp.jpg
items.why: A group portrait where everyone paid to be included, arranged around a corpse. The dissected arm is anatomically wrong.

items.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
items.file: 1665 Girl with a Pearl Earring.jpg
items.why: Not a portrait but a *tronie* — a study of a type rather than a person. Nobody knows who she was, and the pearl may be too large to be a pearl.

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.file: Jheronimus Bosch 097 exterior 02.jpg
items.why: Saint Bartholomew holds his own flayed skin, and the face on the skin is Michelangelo’s. The nudes were painted over with drapery after his death.

items.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
items.file: The Garden of Earthly Delights by Bosch High Resolution 2.jpg
items.why: A triptych that gets stranger as it goes right: Eden, then a vast garden of naked delight, then hell — where a man has sheet music tattooed on his backside.

items.title: Arnolfini Portrait
items.file: Van Eyck - Arnolfini Portrait.jpg
items.why: The convex mirror at the back shows two more figures in the doorway, and above it van Eyck wrote "Jan van Eyck was here" — a signature as witness statement.

items.title: Ghent Altarpiece
items.file: Ghent Altarpiece by Jan van Eyck ALL.jpg
items.why: Probably the most stolen artwork in history. One panel taken in 1934 has never been recovered, and what hangs in its place is a copy.

items.title: The Milkmaid
items.file: Johannes Vermeer - Het melkmeisje - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: A kitchen maid pouring milk, given the gravity of an altarpiece. Vermeer painted perhaps thirty-five pictures in his life.

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.file: Last Judgement (Michelangelo).jpg
items.why: Saint Bartholomew holds his own flayed skin, and the face on the skin is Michelangelo’s. The nudes were painted over with drapery after his death.

items.title: The Creation of Adam
items.file: The Creation of Adam perspective fix.jpg
items.why: On a ceiling, sixty feet up, painted standing. The shape enclosing God has been read since the 1990s as an anatomical cross-section of the human brain.

items.title: The School of Athens
items.file: "The School of Athens" by Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino.jpg
items.why: Plato points up to the ideal, Aristotle levels his hand at the world in front of him — the entire argument of Western philosophy staged as two hand gestures.

items.title: The Scream
items.collection: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design
items.file: Edvard Munch, 1893, The Scream, oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard, 91 x 73 cm, National Gallery of Norway.jpg
items.why: Munch said the sky turned "blood red" over Oslo and he felt an infinite scream passing through nature. The figure is not screaming — it is holding its ears against one.

items.title: The Tower of Babel
items.file: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - The Tower of Babel (Vienna) - Google Art Project - edited.jpg
items.why: Built on the bones of the Roman Colosseum, and the lower storeys are already crumbling while the top is still going up.

items.title: Water Lilies
items.file: Claude Monet Seerosen um 1915 Neue Pinakothek-4.jpg
items.why: Around 250 canvases over the last thirty years of his life, many painted while cataracts took his sight. The late ones run red, which is roughly how the world looked through those lenses.

items.title: The Card Players
items.file: Paul Cézanne, Les joueurs de carte (1892-95).jpg
items.why: Five versions, and nothing happens in any of them — no stakes on the table, no drama, barely any eye contact. The stillness is the subject.

items.title: Sunflowers
items.file: Vincent Willem van Gogh 127.jpg
items.why: Painted to decorate the room he was preparing for Gauguin in Arles — hospitality, before it all went wrong.

items.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
items.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
items.file: Katsushika Hokusai - The Great Wave off the Coast of Kanagawa LCCN2008660568.jpg
items.why: One impression of thousands from the same woodblocks, made to sell cheaply. Hokusai was around seventy, and the mountain in the trough is Fuji.

items.title: Las Hilanderas
items.file: Velazquez-las hilanderas.jpg
items.why: Women spinning in the front room; behind them, lit differently, a tapestry of the Arachne myth. The everyday and the mythic sharing one space.

items.title: The Surrender of Brea
items.file: Velazquez-The Surrender of Breda.jpg
items.why: The victor reaches out to stop the defeated commander from kneeling. Spanish calls it Las Lanzas, after the forest of pikes behind.

items.title: The Clothed Maja
items.collection: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando
items.file: Goya Maja ubrana2.jpg

items.title: The Second of May 1808
items.file: El dos de mayo de 1808 en Madrid.jpg

items.title: Charles IV of Spain and His Family
items.file: La familia de Carlos IV, por Francisco de Goya.jpg
items.why: The royal family rendered without a shred of flattery. Goya put himself at his easel in the shadows on the left, exactly as Velázquez had.

items.title: Sleeping Venus
items.file: Giorgione - Sleeping Venus - Google Art Project 2.jpg
items.why: Left unfinished when Giorgione died young; Titian is generally thought to have completed the landscape. Nearly every reclining nude since descends from this pose.

items.title: Assumption of the Virgin
items.file: Tizian 041.jpg

items.title: Sacred and Profane Love
items.file: Tiziano - Amor Sacro y Amor Profano (Galería Borghese, Roma, 1514)FXD.jpg

items.title: The Coronation of Napoleon
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Le Sacre de Napoléon - Jacques-Louis David - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3699 ; MR 1437.jpg
items.why: He has already crowned himself and is in the act of crowning Joséphine. His mother sits prominently in the stands; she refused to attend, and David painted her in regardless.

items.title: The Sleeping Gypsy
items.file: La Bohémienne endormie.jpg

items.title: L'Absinthe
items.file: Edgar Degas - In a Café - Google Art Project 2.jpg
items.why: Denounced as ugly and degrading when it reached London. The two models were a friend and an actress, neither of them drinkers.

items.title: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
items.file: La decapitación de San Juan Bautista, por Caravaggio.jpg
items.why: The only painting Caravaggio ever signed — and he signed it in the blood running from the neck.

items.title: The Fortune Teller
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: The Fortune Teller-Caravaggio (Louvre).jpg

items.title: Self-Portrait as Bacchus
items.file: Young Sick Bacchus-Caravaggio (1593).jpg

items.title: Supper at Emmaus
items.file: Caravaggio — Supper at Emmaus.jpg

items.title: Bacchus
items.file: Baco, por Caravaggio.jpg

items.title: Supper at Emmaus
items.file: Caravaggio - Supper at Emmaus - National Gallery London.jpeg

items.title: Death of the Virgin
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Death of the Virgin-Caravaggio (1606).jpg

items.title: Amor Vincit Omnia
items.file: Caravaggio - Cupid as Victor - Google Art Project.jpg

items.title: Annunciation
items.collection: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy
items.file: Caravaggio - The Annunciation.JPG
items.why: An early work, and the Virgin’s right arm is far too long — it resolves correctly only if you stand below and to the right, which is where it originally hung.

items.title: Grande Odalisque
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: La grande odalisque - Jean-Auguste Dominique Ingres - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 1158.jpg
items.why: Critics said she had no bones. Her spine has since been measured as carrying roughly three vertebrae too many, which is exactly why the pose flows the way it does.

ref.what: Do women have to be naked to get into the Met. Museum?

items.title: The Turkish Bath
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Le Bain Turc, by Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres, from C2RMFFXD.jpg

items.title: The Massacre at Chios
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Scène des massacres de Scio, Eugène Delacroix - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3823 ; C3.jpg

items.title: Death of Sardanapalus
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: La Mort de Sardanapale - Eugène Delacroix - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 2346.jpg
items.why: A king having everything he owns destroyed in front of him as he dies. The reception was hostile enough to set Delacroix back years.

items.title: The Painter's Studio
items.file: Courbet LAtelier du peintre.jpg
items.why: Subtitled “a real allegory”, which is a contradiction on purpose. He paints a landscape in the centre while his supporters fill one half of the room and the world fills the other.

items.title: A Burial at Ornans
items.file: Gustave Courbet - A Burial at Ornans - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: A village funeral, painted at the scale reserved for kings and battles. The size was the scandal, not the subject.

items.title: The Yellow Christ
items.file: Paul Gauguin - The Yellow Christ (Le Christ jaune) 1889.jpg
items.why: A Breton wayside crucifix set in a Breton field among Breton women, painted in flat blocks with the modelling stripped out of it.

items.title: When Will You Marry?
items.file: Paul Gauguin, Nafea Faa Ipoipo? (When Will You Marry?) 1892, oil on canvas, 101 x 77 cm.jpg
items.why: Painted in Tahiti in his first year there. Reported in 2015 to have sold for the highest price ever paid for a painting, though the figure was later disputed.

items.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
items.file: Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Luncheon of the Boating Party - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: His actual friends, posed over several months at a riverside restaurant. The woman playing with the little dog married him.

items.title: Music in the Tuileries
items.file: MANET - Música en las Tullerías (National Gallery, Londres, 1862).jpg

items.title: The Balcony
items.file: Edouard Manet - The Balcony - Google Art Project.jpg

items.title: The Blind Leading the Blind
items.file: Bruegel, Pieter (I) - Blind leading the blind Google Art Project.jpeg
items.why: Six blind men going into a ditch one after another. The eye conditions are painted precisely enough that ophthalmologists have diagnosed them individually.

items.title: The Triumph of Death
items.file: The Triumph of Death by Pieter Bruegel the Elder.jpg
items.why: An army of skeletons harvesting the living. In one corner a game of backgammon carries on regardless, which is both the joke and the horror.

items.title: The Peasant Wedding
items.file: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Peasant Wedding - Google Art Project.jpg

items.title: The Sea of Ice
items.file: Friedrich, Caspar David - Eismeer.jpg

items.title: Adoration of the Magi
items.file: Zanobi-Altar.jpg
items.why: Abandoned unfinished when he left Florence for Milan. Beneath the calm foreground the underdrawing holds a cavalry battle and a ruin.

items.title: Venus and Mars
items.file: Venus and Mars.jpg

items.title: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz
items.file: El Greco - The Burial of the Count of Orgaz.JPG

items.title: Death of the Virgin
items.file: 1462 Mantegna Der Tod Mariens Museo del Prado anagoria.jpg

items.title: Lamentation of Christ
items.file: Lamentación sobre Cristo muerto, por Andrea Mantegna.jpg
items.why: Foreshortened from the soles of the feet. The feet are painted smaller than true perspective demands, because true perspective would have made them monstrous.

items.title: The Tempest
items.file: Giorgione - Das Gewitter.jpg
items.why: Nobody has ever agreed what is happening in it. X-rays found a nude woman underneath the soldier, so Giorgione appears not to have been certain either.

items.title: The Wedding at Cana
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Les Noces de Cana - Paolo Veronese - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 142 ; MR 384.jpg
items.why: The largest painting in the Louvre. Napoleon’s troops cut it in half to carry it out of Venice.

items.title: Annunciation
items.file: Annunciation Memling.jpg
items.why: An early work, and the Virgin’s right arm is far too long — it resolves correctly only if you stand below and to the right, which is where it originally hung.

items.title: Black Square (1915)
items.file: Чёрный супрематический квадрат. 1915. ГТГ.png
items.why: Hung across the corner of the room in 1915 — the position a Russian household reserved for its icon. That placement is the argument.

items.title: Barge Haulers on the Volga
items.file: Ilya Repin - Barge Haulers on the Volga - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Eleven men dragging a barge upstream in harness. The young one in the middle, straightening against the strap, is the argument the picture is making.

items.title: The Ninth Wave
items.file: Hovhannes Aivazovsky - The Ninth Wave - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Aivazovsky painted around six thousand seascapes and rarely worked from life — this is all memory and studio.

items.title: Lamentation of Christ
items.file: Rogier van der Weyden 013.1.jpg
items.why: Foreshortened from the soles of the feet. The feet are painted smaller than true perspective demands, because true perspective would have made them monstrous.

items.title: The Descent from the Cross
items.file: El Descendimiento, by Rogier van der Weyden, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg

items.title: Irises
items.file: Irises-Vincent van Gogh.jpg
items.why: Painted in his first week at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, where he called the work a lightning rod for his illness. One iris in the crowd is white.

items.title: The Night Café
items.file: Vincent Willem van Gogh 076.jpg
items.why: He wrote that he had tried to express “the terrible passions of humanity” in red and green, and to paint a place where a man could ruin himself.

items.title: Starry Night Over the Rhone
items.file: Vincent van Gogh - Starry Night - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: A year before The Starry Night, painted on the riverbank after dark — by his own account with candles fixed to his hat brim for light.

items.title: Wheatfield with Crows
items.file: Korenveld met kraaien - s0149V1962 - Van Gogh Museum.jpg
items.why: Often called his last painting; it was not, though it was one of the last. The path in the middle goes nowhere.

items.title: The Baptism of Christ
items.file: Verrocchio and Leonardo, Baptism of Christ, c1470-75, Uffizi.jpg
items.why: The kneeling angel on the left is by Verrocchio’s teenage pupil Leonardo. Vasari claims his master never picked up a brush again.

items.title: Madonna of the Goldfinch
items.file: Raphael, Madonna del Cardellino, 1507, Uffizi.jpg

items.title: La fornarina
items.file: Raffaello Sanzio - La Fornarina (ca. 1519-1520).jpg
items.why: The armband carries Raphael’s own name, which is about as direct a claim on a sitter as painting allows. She is traditionally identified as a baker’s daughter he loved.

items.title: The Marriage of the Virgin
items.file: Raffaello - Spozalizio - Web Gallery of Art.jpg

items.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
items.file: Gustav Klimt, 1907, Adele Bloch-Bauer I, Neue Galerie New York.jpg
items.why: Looted by the Nazis and recovered decades later by the sitter’s niece after a long legal fight — the case that became the film Woman in Gold.

items.title: Danaë
items.file: Gustav Klimt 010.jpg

items.title: Ginevra de' Benci
items.file: Ginevra de' Benci - National Gallery of Art.jpg
items.why: The only Leonardo in the Americas. The panel was cut down at some point, so her hands — which survive in a separate study — are gone.

items.title: Salvator Mundi
items.file: Leonardo da Vinci, Salvator Mundi, c.1500, oil on walnut, 45.4 × 65.6 cm.jpg
items.why: Sold in 2017 for more than any painting in history, and argued over ever since — the crystal orb does not refract what is behind it, which is a strange thing for Leonardo to get wrong.

items.title: Saint John the Baptist
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Leonardo da Vinci - Saint John the Baptist C2RMF retouched.jpg
items.why: His last painting. The raised finger and that smile emerging from total darkness have unsettled viewers for five hundred years.

items.title: The Virgin and Child with Saint Anne
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Sainte Anne Leonard.jpg
items.why: Three generations stacked into a single pyramid, the grown daughter sitting in her mother’s lap. Freud wrote an entire essay about the shape of it.

items.title: Adoration of the Magi
items.file: Leonardo da Vinci, Adoration, c1481, Uffizi.jpg
items.why: Abandoned unfinished when he left Florence for Milan. Beneath the calm foreground the underdrawing holds a cavalry battle and a ruin.

items.title: Annunciation
items.file: Annunciation (Leonardo) (cropped).jpg
items.why: An early work, and the Virgin’s right arm is far too long — it resolves correctly only if you stand below and to the right, which is where it originally hung.

items.title: Doni Tondo
items.file: Tondo Doni 2015.png
items.why: The only finished panel painting by Michelangelo that survives. He designed the frame too, and it counts as part of the work.

items.title: Danaë
items.file: Artemisia Gentileschi - Danaë - 93-1986 - Saint Louis Art Museum.jpg

items.title: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
items.file: Rembrandt Christ in the Storm on the Lake of Galilee.jpg
items.why: His only seascape. Stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in 1990 and never recovered — the empty frame still hangs there.

items.title: Return of the Prodigal Son
items.file: Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn - Return of the Prodigal Son - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: A very late work. The father’s two hands are painted differently — one reads as a man’s, the other as a woman’s.

items.title: Danaë
items.file: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn 026.jpg

items.title: The Jewish Bride
items.file: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn - Portret van een paar als oudtestamentische figuren, genaamd 'Het Joodse bruidje' - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Van Gogh said he would give ten years of his life to sit in front of it for a fortnight with nothing but a crust of bread.

items.title: Belshazzar's Feast
items.file: Rembrandt-Belsazar.jpg

items.title: Woman Holding a Balance
items.file: Johannes Vermeer - Woman Holding a Balance - Google Art Project.jpg

items.title: View of Delft
items.file: Johannes Vermeer - View of Delft - 92 - Mauritshuis.jpg
items.why: Proust thought it the most beautiful painting in the world, and killed off a character in his novel standing in front of it, looking at a small patch of yellow wall.

items.title: The Baptism of Christ
items.file: Piero della Francesca - Battesimo di Cristo (National Gallery, London).jpg
items.why: The kneeling angel on the left is by Verrocchio’s teenage pupil Leonardo. Vasari claims his master never picked up a brush again.

items.why: An early work, and the Virgin’s right arm is far too long — it resolves correctly only if you stand below and to the right, which is where it originally hung.

items.title: The Astronomer
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: Johannes Vermeer - The Astronomer - 1668.jpg
items.why: The globe and the open book are real, identifiable objects, which is how the painting can be dated at all.

items.title: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
items.file: Jan Vermeer van Delft - Brieflezend meisje bij het venster (ca. 1657-59).jpg

items.title: The Art of Painting
items.file: Jan Vermeer - The Art of Painting - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: He never sold it, and his widow tried to keep it from the creditors when he died. It later passed through Hitler’s collection.

items.title: The Little Street
items.file: Johannes Vermeer - Gezicht op huizen in Delft, bekend als 'Het straatje' - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: One of only two Vermeer cityscapes. A 2015 study of Delft’s canal-tax records proposed an exact address for it.

items.title: Danaë
items.file: Correggio 008.jpg

items.title: Virgin of the Rocks
items.file: Leonardo Da Vinci - Vergine delle Rocce (Louvre).jpg
items.why: There are two, in Paris and in London. The likeliest account is that he painted one, fell out with the commissioners over money, and painted another.

items.title: Madonna
items.file: Edvard Munch - Madonna (1894-1895).jpg
items.why: Not a Madonna in any conventional sense. Some versions carry a foetus and sperm in the frame itself, which tells you plainly what he thought he was painting.

items.title: Black Paintings
items.file: Quintasordo.svg

items.title: Isle of the Dead
items.file: Arnold Böcklin - Die Toteninsel III (Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin).jpg

items.title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
items.file: David - Napoleon crossing the Alps - Malmaison2.jpg
items.why: He made the crossing on a mule, in fair weather, behind a guide. He instructed David to paint him “calm on a fiery horse”, and David did.

ref.what: Napoleon Leading the Army over the Alps

items.title: Danaë
items.file: Tizian 011.jpg

items.title: Portrait paintings of Dr. Gachet
items.file: Portrait of Dr. Gachet.jpg
items.why: Painted in the last weeks of his life, of the doctor treating him. Van Gogh wrote that Gachet seemed sicker than he was.

items.title: Bedroom in Arles
items.file: Vincent van Gogh - De slaapkamer - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: Three versions exist. He wanted flat colour to suggest rest and absolute calm, and skewed the perspective deliberately to get it.

items.title: Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks
items.file: Ilja Jefimowitsch Repin - Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks - Yorck.jpg
items.why: They are composing a gleefully obscene reply to the Ottoman Sultan. Repin spent twelve years on it, and the real subject is the laughter.

items.title: Benois Madonna
items.file: Leonardo, Madonna Benois.JPG
items.why: An early work that disappeared for centuries and resurfaced in Russia, reportedly in the keeping of a travelling musician.

items.title: The Yellow House
items.file: Vincent van Gogh - The yellow house ('The street').jpg
items.why: The house in Arles he rented for the artists’ colony he had been planning for years. The colony lasted nine weeks and ended with his ear.

items.title: The Red Vineyard
items.file: Vincent van Gogh - Red Vineyard at Arles (1888).jpg
items.why: Long described as the only painting he sold in his lifetime. That claim is probably too strong, but this one did sell, months before he died.

items.title: The Church at Auvers
items.file: Vincent van Gogh - The Church in Auvers-sur-Oise, View from the Chevet - Google Art Project.jpg
items.why: From his final weeks. The building is painted without a visible way in.

items.title: La Belle Ferronnière
items.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
items.file: La Belle Ferronière - Google Arts.jpg
items.why: Nobody knows who she is. The title is an eighteenth-century filing error — it belongs to a different sitter altogether.

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.file: William-Adolphe Bouguereau (1825-1905) - The Birth of Venus (1879).jpg
items.why: She is not being born but arriving, blown ashore on a shell. Painted on canvas when Florence still expected panel, which is part of why it survived.

items.title: Ivan the Terrible and his son Ivan on November 16, 1581
items.file: Iván el Terrible y su hijo, por Iliá Repin.jpg
items.why: The instant after the blow, with the father’s face doing all the work. The Tsar banned it from display, and visitors have attacked it twice since.

items.title: The Sleepers
items.collection: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris
items.file: Gustave Courbet - Le Sommeil (1866), Paris, Petit Palais.jpg
items.why: Two women asleep together, painted for a private collector and kept out of public view for decades.

items.title: Sunset at Montmajour
items.file: Sunset at Montmajour 1888 Van Gogh.jpg
items.why: Attributed to Van Gogh, then dismissed as a fake and left in an attic for most of a century, then re-authenticated in 2013.

items.title: Morning in a Pine Forest
items.file: Shishkin, Ivan - Morning in a Pine Forest.jpg
items.why: Shishkin painted the forest; another artist, Savitsky, painted the bears. The dealer wiped Savitsky’s signature off the canvas.

items.title: Madonna of the Carnation
items.file: LEONARDO-DA-VINCI - MADONNA-MIT-DER-NELKE-7779 917154 BSTGS.jpg
items.why: Early Leonardo, and the Virgin’s face has a slumped, slightly melted quality — the result of him experimenting with the paint itself.

items.title: Madonna Litta
items.file: Leonardo da Vinci attributed - Madonna Litta.jpg
items.why: The attribution is argued over. The design and the drapery look like Leonardo; the handling of the child, to many eyes, does not.
